description: HexLattice::from_rings builds a 2-ring lattice whose central tile [n_rings-1,n_rings-1] receives outer-ring element index 3 instead of the single inner-ring element. Confirmed for BOTH orientations at n_rings=2: with outer ring [10,11,12,13,14,15] and inner [42], universe_at(centre)=13 (=outer[3]) not 42; the inner element lands off-centre (e.g. X orientation puts it at [2,0]). The geometry methods (center_offset/get_indices/get_local_position/distance) are CORRECT — the bug is purely in the ring->tile fill walk (fill_lattice_x src/lattice.cpp:546, fill_lattice_y :598) and/or the outer-first flatten order from_rings feeds them. The existing 4-ring y notebook test did not catch it because every ring's first element AND the inner ring all share the value 1, so a mis-slotted centre still reads 1. NEEDS the canonical OpenMC src/lattice.cpp fill_lattice_x/y to diff against (not available on this build host) before fixing, per the crate's mirror-canonical-source rule. Found while adding op-6tz.31 (X round-trip test); that test and the new from_rings_3d test both deliberately avoid asserting intra-level fill placement.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Fixed in 590b0e0. Root cause: from_rings/from_rings_3d fed outer-ring-first input to the row-order fill_lattice_x/y walk (spatial rows, not hex rings) → central element mis-placed onto an outer tile; the whole placement was a non-round-tripping permutation. Fix: geometry-derived placement (fill_level via ring_slots/tile_ring/tile_xy) — per hex-radius k, sort that ring's skewed tiles by planar angle (+x start, CCW) and map ring elements onto them; proven bijection over all hexagon tiles, so universe_at(get_indices(tile_centre)) round-trips. New tests ring_fill_round_trip_{x,y} + from_rings_3d_single_level_matches_2d; 158 lib + 27 notebook tests pass. CAVEAT: within-ring +x-start CCW angular convention is best-effort per OpenMC's 'each ring starts along +x' doc; a line-by-line diff vs openmc/lattice.py is still owed. Round-trip correctness + valid bijection verified; NOT claimed OpenMC-bit-identical.

title: outram-mc: fill_lattice_x/y misplace ring elements for small ring counts

description: multi_region::mesh_to_mesh::MappingMethod::CellVolumeWeight currently approximates upstream's imCellVolumeWeight as nearest-cell addressing + a global integral rescale (globally conservative, not exact local overlap). Exact upstream integrates true polyhedral cell-overlap volumes (supermesh intersection). Needs a basic-lib supermesh/mesh-clipping operator (AABB octree + polyhedron clipping). Until then the degraded mode is documented and conserves the volume integral.
title: genfoam multiRegion: exact conservative meshToMesh (imCellVolumeWeight polyhedral overlap)

description:
The 160 W/(m2 K) pebble-to-helium coefficient is invented. Wiring KTA friction (op-szmi.8) surfaced a quantitative check on it: at that value the bed sits 204.7 K above bulk helium, against Gao & Shi 2002 Table 2's PEAK fuel-to-coolant difference of 100.7 K at 100% load (918.7 / 876.7 / 818 degC max fuel / fuel-surface / coolant). A bed AVERAGE must be below the peak, so the coefficient is low by roughly 2-3x.

Left unchanged deliberately during op-szmi.8 -- re-anchoring is a modelling decision needing its own V&V, not a side effect of wiring friction.

Route: KTA 3102.2 Nu correlation, transcribed in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-plant-data.md 7.3. NOTE the OCR caveat on one symbol recorded there -- verify against the source before trusting the transcription.
title: htgr_sim_v1: re-anchor pebble-to-helium HTC against Gao & Shi Table 2

description:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-12 in tampines-steam-tables (the coolprop half is the sibling agent's).

FIXED for TampinesSteamArray: added `set_inlet_mass_flowrate` / `clear_inlet_mass_flowrate` (additive API, no signature changes), implementing OpenFOAM's flowRateInletVelocity. The inlet velocity is re-derived every pressure corrector from the SAME interpolated inlet-face density that then multiplies it to form the boundary mass flux, so the imposed flux is exactly m_dot by construction. `set_inlet_velocity` clears it and vice versa, so the two cannot silently fight over the same patch.

MEASURED (test `prescribed_inlet_mass_flowrate_is_imposed_exactly`), 8 cells, 4 MPa water, target 3.2 kg/s:
  prescribed mass-flow inlet : 3.200000000 kg/s (+0.0000%)
  velocity from CORRECT rho  : 3.200148121 kg/s (+0.0046%)
  velocity from WRONG rho    : 2.583169047 kg/s (-19.2760%)

STILL OPEN: `set_mass_flowrate` itself remains inert bookkeeping. It was deliberately NOT made active -- doing so would silently change behaviour for existing callers who set it for bookkeeping, which is a behavioural breaking change on a published crate. Its doc comment now says plainly that it is not a boundary condition and points at set_inlet_mass_flowrate. Whether to deprecate or repurpose it is a maintainer call.
title: Fluid arrays have no mass-flow boundary condition; velocity BC lets the solved flow drift from the metered one
